_description: Re-measurement of the 5 proposed fixes from the 2026-10-01 pi5_benchmark run, on the same Raspberry Pi 5 Model B Rev 1.0. Each value below was actually run, not estimated.

ocr_decoder.hypothesis: greedy decoder should be faster than beamsearch (beamWidth=5)
ocr_decoder.result: regressed - greedy measured slower, not faster
ocr_decoder.note: The ~19s cost is EasyOCR's text-detector network on CPU, not the beam-search decode step, so the decoder flag doesn't touch the actual bottleneck. config.OCR_DECODER left at 'beamsearch' (env-overridable).

bn.measured_on_phrase: the OCR capture confirmation sentence (লেখা সংরক্ষণ করা হয়েছে। শুনতে রিড বাটন চাপুন), NOT the currency denomination phrase - see currency_denomination_tts_correction below for the phrase currency mode actually speaks.
bn.reason: piper 2023.11.14-2 (only prebuilt ARM64 release) throws 'Phonemes must be one codepoint' on bn_BD-google-medium.onnx (e.g. the diphthong "aɪ" is not a single codepoint in this binary's phoneme id map) and aborts. utils.TTSEngine._piper() now checks piper's return code and falls back to espeak-ng, so Bangla still speaks - just at the unchanged espeak-ng speed.

playback_fix.problem: On this headless Pi 5 (no display attached), PipeWire has nothing to route the HDMI ALSA device to, so 'aplay' fails to open it (error 524) on every call - and neither that failure nor the piper crash above raised a Python exception, so TTSEngine._piper() would previously return having played nothing at all, silently.
playback_fix.fix: utils.TTSEngine._audio_player_cmd() probes 'aplay' then 'pw-cat' once per process and caches whichever one actually opens the device; _piper() also now checks piper_proc.returncode and raises (triggering the espeak-ng fallback) instead of assuming success.

object_mode.before: skipped - no YOLOv8 COCO weights in this checkout

watermark_localizer.claim_checked: live app already uses the learned localizer, not SIFT, by default
watermark_localizer.evidence: WatermarkChecker.localizer loads whenever config.WATERMARK_LOCALIZER_PATH exists (it does); genuine_prob() calls _window_learned() first and only falls back to SIFT when that returns None. The benchmark's 372ms 'watermark_int8_sift' entry forced checker.localizer=None for comparison - it does not reflect live app behavior.

currency_int8.claim_checked: live app already loads best_int8.onnx on Pi 5, not best.pt
currency_int8.evidence: config.CURRENCY_YOLO_PATH already selects best_int8.onnx when config.ON_RASPBERRY_PI_5 is true, and _candidate_yolo_paths() inserts it first. Confirmed by live log on this device: 'Currency YOLO loaded from .../best_int8.onnx'. The benchmark's separate taka_yolo_pt/taka_yolo_onnx_fp32 entries are explicit comparison loads, not what currency_mode_full actually runs.

ocr_canvas_size.hypothesis: EasyOCR's detector upscales toward canvas_size (default 2560) before running CRAFT; the glass's 640px camera frame doesn't need that, so a smaller canvas_size should be faster with no accuracy loss.

single_frame_timing.note: n=1 per setting, synthetic text_frame() from benchmark_pi5.py, beamsearch decoder

accuracy_spotcheck.note: reduced sample (n=16: 8 bn + 8 en, half with rotation/blur/downscale wild augmentation), same phrases and same random draws at both canvas sizes for a fair controlled comparison - NOT the full 80-sample scripts/eval_ocr_offline.py methodology, and used NotoSansBengali.ttf (Linux) rather than the original Windows Vrinda font, so these numbers are not directly comparable to results/ocr_cer.json's published baseline. Run the full eval yourself (now canvas_size-aware via config.OCR_CANVAS_SIZE) for a thesis-grade number.

ocr_canvas_size.status: promising, not adopted as default - config.OCR_CANVAS_SIZE added (default stays 2560) pending the full eval_ocr_offline.py run. Override with OCR_CANVAS_SIZE=640 to try it.
ocr_canvas_size.how_to_validate_fully: cd savior_glass && OCR_CANVAS_SIZE=2560 python3 scripts/eval_ocr_offline.py  (baseline, ~27 min at n=80) and OCR_CANVAS_SIZE=640 python3 scripts/eval_ocr_offline.py (candidate, ~9 min) - compare results/ocr_offline_repaired.json between runs.

currency_denomination_tts_correction.error_found: the first pass's 'Currency end-to-end' and 'TTS Bangla dominates currency' figures used the OCR confirmation sentence's TTS duration (6.19s) as a stand-in for the currency announcement's TTS duration. They are different, much shorter phrases - this was a measurement mistake, not an app bug. Corrected 2026-10-01.
currency_denomination_tts_correction.actual_phrases_spoken_by_currency_mode: config._DENOMINATION_BN in modes/currency_mode.py, e.g. 'duI TakAr note' (2 taka) through 'eka hAjAr TakAr note' (1000 taka) - all 3-4 words

measured_espeak_ng_bn_s135.note: single-sample timings, not a full median/p95 sweep like the other TTS numbers in this file - but real() time is almost entirely audio playback duration (user+sys CPU time is ~0.01-0.04s each run), so variance across repeats is expected to be small, unlike compute-bound measurements.

ocr_capture.change: process_frame unchanged; TTS confirmation now via Piper (en-us)

currency.change: unchanged either way - both inference (already int8) and TTS (Bangla, espeak-ng) are the same path as before. The 'before' number itself was wrong (see currency_denomination_tts_correction); it was never 6.5s.
currency.basis: 326.62ms (currency_mode_full median) + 2586ms (500 taka denomination TTS, representative of the 1978-2586ms range across denominations)
